guide.summary: Internal app on your own workspace (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none); Public agent for many customer workspaces (app review).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Internal app on your own workspace (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none). Hardest: Public agent for many customer workspaces (app review).

composio.note: Composio has a managed Slack OAuth app for prototypes. For production, use your own client ID and secret in a Composio auth config; copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

need_own_app.answer: For prototypes, no: Composio's managed Slack app works. For production, yes, so users see your app name rather than Composio's, and you get your own scopes and a dedicated quota.
reasons: Consent screen shows Composio with the managed app
Custom scopes need your own app
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum trigger polling interval
Marketplace listing requires your own app

prerequisites.title: Slack workspace and app settings access
prerequisites.detail: You create the app at api.slack.com/apps; scopes are added in its settings.

prerequisites.title: 10 active installs before submitting
prerequisites.detail: Marketplace submission requires at least 10 active workspace installs, kept for the whole review. Real users on multiple workspaces are needed first.

prerequisites.title: Listing assets and public pages
prerequisites.detail: You need a public landing page, privacy policy with a contact method, support page and 1600x1000 listing images.

steps.title: Create Slack app and add scopes
steps.detail: Create the app at api.slack.com/apps and add the minimum scopes. Mark scopes optional where possible.
steps.done_when: App exists with client ID and secret.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config via Composio's API with your client ID and secret. Add the Composio redirect URI (must be HTTPS) to Slack's Redirect URLs.
steps.done_when: OAuth connection completes for a test user.

steps.title: Draft per-scope justifications
steps.detail: Write a reason for each scope explaining how the app uses it. Remove scopes for unbuilt features.
steps.done_when: Every scope has a usage explanation.

steps.title: Get 10 active workspace installs
steps.detail: Recruit real users across workspaces to install the app.

steps.title: Prepare listing, pages and security info
steps.detail: Publish the landing, privacy and support pages, produce images, and complete security and AI disclosures.

steps.title: Submit and wait for review
steps.detail: Slack reviews the app. Fixes in the preliminary stage reportedly reset your place in the queue.

traps.title: The temporary authorization code expires after ten minutes
traps.detail: The temporary authorization code expires after ten minutes.

traps.title: Support requests are expected to receive a response within
traps.detail: Support requests are expected to receive a response within 2 business days.

traps.title: Apps installed on fewer than 10 active workspaces and
traps.detail: Apps installed on fewer than 10 active workspaces and with fewer than 10 weekly active users are unsuitable for the Marketplace.

traps.title: Review can take 4-6 months
traps.detail: Docs give no duration. Developers report 152 days to first feedback and about four months total.

traps.title: Install count must hold during review
traps.detail: Falling below 10 installed workspaces during review breaks the requirement.

traps.title: Broad scopes get enhanced review or rejection
traps.detail: History, search and admin scopes are scrutinised or unlikely to be approved. User token scopes used unnecessarily are returned.

traps.title: Fixes reset queue place
traps.detail: Fixes during the preliminary stage reset your queue position, so polish before submitting.

traps.title: Unapproved scopes block install of published apps
traps.detail: A published app cannot be installed while its requested scopes are in review or unsubmitted.

traps.title: Non-listed app only works on its own workspace
traps.detail: An undistributed app can only be installed on the workspace that owns it.

traps.title: Managed app shows Composio name
traps.detail: Users see 'Composio wants to access your account' with the managed app.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: I submitted at the beginning of January and got approval in May — so the review alone took four months
evidence.answer: One developer's blog report (2026): the Marketplace review alone took about four months, from submission in early January to approval in May.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: It took Slack 152 days to respond to me with feedback as part of round 1 of their marketplace submission process.
evidence.answer: One developer's LinkedIn post reports Slack took 152 days to return round-1 feedback on a Marketplace submission.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: In short, if you submit a slack app to the marketplace today, expect to be unpublished for at least the next 6 months.
evidence.answer: The same developer expects at least about six months before a submitted Slack app is published; they report round 2 is far quicker.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Slack asks about every scope separately. There's no "I took it just in case" option.
evidence.answer: Reviewers ask for a justification of each scope separately, so requesting unused scopes adds review friction.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Slack states plainly in the confirmation email that at this stage every fix resets your place in the queue.
evidence.answer: Fixes made during the preliminary stage reset the submission's place in the queue, so polish listing and pages before submitting.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: If a change required a new scope, it could mean going back through verification.
evidence.answer: A developer reports that post-launch changes adding a new scope may trigger another review; changes within already-approved scopes shipped without one.
